overall: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law when the chair polled members by email and phone on a subdivision plan, deliberating outside a posted meeting. Bias and ethics claims were declined.

allegations.summary: Chair allegedly polled other members by email and phone on a subdivision plan around July 10, deliberating outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Through his email to other Board members and ensuing separate telephone calls, Mr. Golden engaged in prohibited serial communication, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged personal bias and ethical violations by the chair, which the complainant said went beyond the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: The allegations of personal bias and ethical violations, even if true, would not constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law and we therefore decline to review those complaints.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements, with a caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law’s requirements and caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
